integration_obligations: Run guarded normal/nonzero/signal/failed-exec/cancellation/timeout/memory/output-overflow cases before using this wrapper for accepted measurements. The metadata tests use fake OS/process calls only.
Verify actual descriptor transport and source/report exclusion, stdout/stdin behavior, sealing and process cleanup under the existing guard.
Keep exact production executable/receipt, generator, frozen matrix/cell/revision, metric configuration and guard evidence bindings in the future caller and independent resource validator.
Keep MiniKQL allocation/peak instrumentation and operator-consumption timing separate. This wrapper alone does not fulfill Q01 resource acceptance.
metric_limits: CPU and Linux ru_maxrss describe the waited child lifetime including fork/exec/startup/setup and kernel-attributed waited descendants. They are not operator-only interval measurements.
Linux ru_maxrss is a kernel high-water measurement, not summed concurrent scope RSS. Descendants that are not included by kernel wait accounting cannot be inferred from it.
Python wrapper-parent CPU is excluded, but pre-exec/startup floors may dominate small target measurements. Future paired admission must require sufficient measured signal.
Loaded-helper/source identity relies on the existing source-freeze discipline, while the child wrapper itself executes the exact sealed source snapshot.
reviewed_contracts: Positive-PID wait4 selects the exact launched child; subprocess.returncode is set from that same terminal wait status. No cumulative RUSAGE_CHILDREN subtraction is used.

Target process gets only original payload descriptors; measurement source and report descriptors are excluded by close_fds/pass_fds. Cwd, environment, session and rlimits are inherited from the existing guarded worker.
Existing run_anonymous receives guard options unchanged; wrapper and child remain in its scope, and the caller must retain the serial lease.

Normal and nonzero exits preserve their codes. A naturally signaled child yields a sealed report, then the wrapper restores/unblocks and re-raises the same signal so the existing guard retains 128+signal mapping.

A Python interruption kills and reaps the exact child before propagating. Default fatal signals bypass that local handler, but the existing outer guard still owns scope-wide cleanup and rejects stopped/incomplete runs.

A fresh bounded sealed memfd contains numeric metadata only. Parent requires exact report keys, nonce, terminal raw status and consistent exit/signal fields. Missing/malformed report, guard stop, overflow, incomplete cleanup or changed file bindings cannot produce raw_observation status.
All semantic/resource-scaling/optimization acceptance flags are hard false. Raw observations can retain natural nonzero exits and are not acceptance evidence.
